name: US HOA, condo and co-op association assessments and capital repairs

notes.insurgent: Fannie 15% reserve floor (Jan 2027) plus Florida SIRS force assessments; no funded association-finance startup. Needs lien-law and lending-license check.
notes.growth: Best combo: $124B assessments, Fannie 15% reserve rule Jan 2027, Florida no-waiver funding, no funded financing player. Check hidden association lenders.

name: US building-permit plan review and inspection (government and private providers)

notes.insurgent: Fresh FL/CA private-provider laws with deemed approval shift volume faster than departments can hire. Licensed review fees fund service first, software scales it.
notes.growth: FL/CA/TX deemed-approval laws outrun understaffed departments; licensed private provider plus software is clear, but labor-based margins cap value.

name: Gas-turbine fleet services and aftermarket (maintenance, repair, parts, upgrades, LTSAs)

notes.insurgent: OEM slots sold to 2031 force owners to keep old frames running; no funded startup. Marketplace, LTSA audit and outage staffing are open.
notes.growth: Sold-out OEM slots force old frames to keep running; no funded independent MRO startup; size spans $10-30B and independents exist.

name: US community associations' (condo/HOA) reserve and capital-repair funding, Florida structural mandate first

notes.insurgent: Same condo-reserve financing wedge as the HOA pool; deadlines passed and special assessments hitting owners, no funded lender.
notes.growth: Same business as P013 via reserves; Florida deadline now past; financing and procurement gap real, Vantaca funded only on software.

name: US OEM and prime purchases of metal castings from foundries (defense-critical)

notes.insurgent: Casting capacity is a genuine bottleneck and nobody funded, but qualification takes years and the DoD plan has no new dollars.
notes.growth: Primary $53.7B revenue; Pentagon calls castings a single point of failure; only Fabri funded; capital and qualification are the real barriers.

name: US health plans' and self-funded employers' out-of-network payments through No Surprises Act arbitration (IDR awards)

notes.insurgent: IDR payouts tripled to $15B, QPA just ruled unlawful, payers lose 85% and self-funded employers have no tooling. Legislative overhaul is the risk.
notes.growth: Volume tripled to $15B and QPA ruled defective, but vendor fees are a fraction, HaloMD holds provider side, Congress could cap awards.

name: US farmers' spend on equipment repair, maintenance and parts

notes.insurgent: Deere settlement strips the diagnostic moat; dealers' 70%-margin service is exposed and no funded independent network exists. Tool access unproven until entered.
notes.growth: Deere settlement is court-backed, dealers' high-margin service exposed, no funded independent repair platform; tool access unproven until order entered.

name: US purchases of power and distribution transformers (utilities, developers, data centers, industrials)

notes.insurgent: Tariffs and 160-week lead times strand utilities; repair, spares pooling and used-unit trading have budget. Repair needs plant capital.
notes.growth: Tariffs plus ~30% supply deficit, new capacity not before 2027-28; funded only in solid-state hardware; repair, spares pooling, standard-spec aggregation open.

name: Captives, group captives and fronting: corporate premium moving out of the commercial market

notes.insurgent: Brokers conflicted against mid-size fleets and nothing venture-funded; group captives need fronting capacity and insurance expertise. Shock is soft pricing, not crisis.
notes.growth: Marsh-reported $79B premium, 118 new captives; fee pool $2-4B is hypothesis; no funded group-captive or fronting platform; heavy capital moat.

name: Utilities' and developers' outsourced transmission and distribution engineering and line-construction contracts

notes.insurgent: Utility capex is huge and growth is hiring-gated; distribution-design automation and public-power engineering have budget. Utility standards and procurement slow.
notes.growth: Huge $31B floor, hiring-gated incumbents; engineering automation and lineworker pipeline unfunded, but Quanta-scale firms thrive and labor is thin-margin.

name: US building owners' spend on fire and life-safety inspection, testing, maintenance and monitoring (POTS copper cutover)

notes.insurgent: FCC copper order plus AT&T retirement forces cutover of fire-alarm lines nationwide; multi-site owners have compliance budgets and roll-ups lack coordination. State licensing needs subcontractors.
notes.growth: Copper cutover forces retrofits, but Resideo-type hardware incumbents and Pye-Barker roll-ups hold the base; one-time work, recurring monitoring is prize.

name: 340B Drug Pricing Program covered-entity purchases (the spread and the rebate transition)

notes.insurgent: Rebate pilot forces hospitals to front full price and prove claims; Kalderos present, litigation could kill it again. Receivable financing needs balance sheet.
notes.growth: Rebate model forces hospitals to front full price, creating financing and data needs; courts and Congress split three ways; spread unsized.

name: Indonesia: free-meals programme (MBG) money flowing from BGN through ~27,000 community kitchens (SPPG) to ingredient suppliers

notes.insurgent: New state payer, 27,000 kitchens, crackdown just landed, nothing funded; bottom-up near $100M. Politics, local presence, and BGN's own marketplace are risks.
notes.growth: New $15B state payer and kitchen crisis, but state is building its own marketplace and program could be cut; $100M needs stacked layers.

name: US biofuel producers' purchases of fats, oils and grease feedstock

notes.insurgent: RFS volumes up 60% and North-American-only 45Z create scarcity rent on domestic fats; origin documentation and collection density are open. Renderers strong.
notes.growth: Strong RFS and 45Z domestic-feedstock shock, no funded players, but renderers like Darling entrenched and roll-up is capital-heavy.

name: Owners' parts and service spend on heavy equipment (ag, construction, mining), opened by right-to-repair

notes.insurgent: Deere order is fresh, but covers Deere ag only, is unproven, and multi-brand diagnostics from Jaltest, Texa exist.
notes.growth: Deere settlement is court-backed but brand-limited; multi-brand diagnostics unfunded; Cat figure is global, independent share unknown.

name: US heavy-duty (Class 6-8) truck repair, maintenance and parts aftermarket

notes.insurgent: Technician scarcity and tariffed parts are real; GPO and mobile technician network are open, but Fullbay and distributors can respond.
notes.growth: Open, fragmented, tariffs and technician shortage; size is stale MacKay data including in-house work; Fullbay proves software entry.

name: US consumer auto-loan interest and fees, with the subprime servicing, collections and repossession layer under stress

notes.insurgent: Tricolor and record delinquencies show thin-ops lenders fail; backup servicing has named payers but small fees. Salient funded, price must beat loss avoided.
notes.growth: Tricolor and record delinquency create backup-servicing need, but servicing spend unsized and lenders thin; round-1 price-versus-value risk.

name: Medicaid home- and community-based services (personal care, home care agencies, fiscal intermediaries)

notes.insurgent: Huge pool and agencies squeezed by H.R.1 and NY consolidation; receivable advances need capital, FI work needs state procurement.
notes.growth: Giant strained pool; receivables advances and statewide FI platforms plausible; shock is cuts that add risk; incumbents and software funded.

name: Airlines' and lessors' spend on commercial aviation MRO and aftermarket parts

notes.insurgent: Engine and casting shortages are real, but PMA/DER approvals are slow and ePlane plus parts distributors are present.
notes.growth: Huge $100B pool and engine MRO bottleneck, OEM parts exclusivity; PMA and used-material path needs inventory capital; marketplaces and AerSale exist.

name: State Medicaid and SNAP agencies' eligibility and administration spend (work requirements, 6-month redeterminations, SNAP admin cost shift)

notes.insurgent: Jan 2027 deadline plus SNAP admin shift; plan-paid retention per member is a real wedge; integrators discount and procurement is slow.
notes.growth: Hard 2027 deadline and SNAP cost shift, but vendor share unsourced, integrators discounting, free EMMY tooling; plan-paid retention is interesting payer.

name: US homeowners insurance premiums in wildfire-, hail- and hurricane-exposed markets (California cat-model reform, Florida reinsurance reset)

notes.insurgent: SIS forces proof of mitigation, a clear evidence-layer gap, but California-only prior-approval and RockRose, Zesty, BurnBot funded.
notes.growth: Verified $173B with California SIS reset, but funded insurtechs and incumbents abound; mitigation-evidence layer and FAIR Plan take-out narrow.

name: US homeowners-insurer-paid property repair and restoration (claims money flowing to contractors)

notes.insurgent: Loss-draft delays and contractor cash gaps are real pain; LA-fire shock is aging and Rebuild is funded. Contractor-paid financing is the entry.
notes.growth: Verified $82B claims money; contractor cash acceleration is a balance-sheet wedge; Rebuild funded, carriers resist payout-raising tools.

name: PJM capacity payments passed through to utilities' and large customers' bills

notes.insurgent: Capacity price at cap three years running gives mid-size C&I real savings; Voltus, CPower, Enel X respond fast.
notes.growth: Fresh $16.4B auction shock, but pass-through is not revenue; Voltus raised $225M, Emerald at $1B; needs storage financing.

name: US prison and jail health care (state corrections departments and counties paying contractors)

notes.insurgent: Wellpath and YesCare failures leave counties without bidders, but liability and clinical-licensing exposure make it hard for a scrappy team.
notes.growth: Incumbent bankruptcies leave counties without bidders, no funded startup; litigation, thin margins, slow procurement; $11B is derived.

name: US medium- and heavy-duty truck parts aftermarket bought by independent fleets and shops

notes.insurgent: Tariffed parts and fragmented shops want price transparency, but Fullbay can add a marketplace and distributors respond.
notes.growth: Floor-quality size (dealers only), 25% tariff since Nov 2025, no funded parts procurement; Fullbay adjacent; margin on flow thin.

name: US state governments' spend on Medicaid and SNAP administration (eligibility determination, enrollment and verification systems, outsourced operations)

notes.insurgent: Same H.R.1 and SNAP shift as P106; per-verification data and MCO-paid retention are real wedges, but vendors discount and states procure slowly.
notes.growth: Duplicate of P106 and P059 as services; same free federal tooling and discounting integrators; vendor share unsourced.

name: US nuclear fleet operating, fuel and capital spend (and the outsourced supplier/services ecosystem behind it)

notes.insurgent: Real policy wave and thin supplier base, but NQA-1 qualification is slow and new-build money mostly lands after 2028.
notes.growth: Shock hits new-build, not the $26B fleet-spend flow; supplier-qualification wedge unclear; Nuclearn and Atomic Canyon only do documentation.

name: US federal agencies' spend on management advisory and professional support services (consultants and support contractors)

notes.insurgent: Civilian consulting cut by a third and T&M under attack, but past-performance and set-aside moats protect incumbents; shock is 18 months old.
notes.growth: Civilian consulting down one-third with outcome-based rebuying, but moats are past performance and set-asides; no funded AI-native civilian delivery firm.

name: US manufactured-home sales and chattel (personal-property) finance

notes.insurgent: GSE chattel channel would reprice the market, but rules are proposals with finality near 2028; Clayton is vertically integrated.
notes.growth: GSE chattel proposal could create a securitizable channel, but not final until 2028; Clayton-owned lenders dominate.

name: US new-home builder sales incentives and mortgage rate buydowns

notes.insurgent: Non-captive mid-size builders lack neutral buydown capital; nothing funded. Concession caps and lender-steering rules need legal check.
notes.growth: Incentive spend real, but third-party buydown slice unsized and captive lenders steer; nobody funded, reachable fees small.

name: US banks' and credit unions' spend on core, digital-banking and processing vendors (Fiserv, FIS, Jack Henry)

notes.insurgent: Fiserv meltdown is rare, but core contracts run decades, vendors run their own conversions, and benchmarking is an existing consulting niche.
notes.growth: Fiserv unraveling real but core replacement is decade-scale; Nymbus, Thought Machine, Mambu funded; conversion-services wedge is small.

name: Clinical laboratory testing (independent, hospital-outreach and reference labs)

notes.insurgent: PAMA cuts have been delayed seven times, so urgency is unreliable; lab underpayment recovery on contingency is real but boutique-served.
notes.growth: PAMA cuts delayed seven times, so shock may fizzle; lab-specific denial recovery unfunded but a normal RCM niche.

name: England social landlords' repairs and maintenance spend (housing associations, Awaab's Law era)

notes.insurgent: Awaab's Law clocks force compliance spend, but Switchee and Mobysoft already sell it. UK housing-association procurement is slow.
notes.growth: Awaab's Law creates UK compliance spend, but margin-starved landlords, Switchee and Mobysoft already serve, UK-only.

name: German Mittelstand ownership succession: purchase-price flow plus advisory and financing fees

notes.insurgent: Size is an upper bound; free nexxt-change substitute, fee layer maybe $1-2B. Roll-up or MBO finance is capital-heavy and German-language.
notes.growth: Demographic cliff real, but fee layer ~$0.5-1.5B and free nexxt-change exists; only an EBO or buy-and-hold vehicle scales.

name: US personal-auto physical-damage claims (collision + comprehensive): insurer payments for repair, parts, calibration and total-loss payouts

notes.insurgent: Policyholder-side total-loss audit has no advocate today; ADAS calibration capacity also open. CCC and Mitchell entrenched, licensing question.
notes.growth: $92B claims pool, but CCC, Mitchell, Solera own workflow; ADAS calibration capacity is the open lane; several AI estimators funded.

name: US OEM spend on outsourced custom machined parts from independent machine shops

notes.insurgent: Hadrian ($7.9B) and Isembard fund the capital side and shop software is crowded; mid-volume niche exists but is contested.
notes.growth: Hadrian at $7.9B validates category but crowds defense CNC; mid-volume commercial parts and buy-and-automate shop roll-ups remain open.

name: US commercial auto and trucking liability premiums

notes.insurgent: CDL and English rules reshape driver risk; Nirvana, Cover Whale, HDVI are funded. Driver-qualification data feed is a plausible wedge.
notes.growth: Nirvana ($1.5B), Cover Whale, HDVI funded; driver-qualification feed real but small; capital and licensing intensive.

name: US packaging extended producer responsibility (EPR) producer fees

notes.insurgent: State EPR fees hit brands from 2026-27; CAA builds data systems from scratch, so SKU-level reporting and invoice audit have clear payers. Litigation pending.
notes.growth: Borderline $5B, California plan still evolving; CAA dominates; SKU-level reporting SaaS plausible but small and litigation-exposed.

name: US importers' customs-duty payments on industrial inputs and the duty-mitigation services market

notes.insurgent: Monthly tariff regime changes make duty recovery and metals-content data recurring; Big 4 and trade counsel already on contingency, licensing check.
notes.growth: Fee slice unsized, refund and audit work episodic; Altana, Flexport, brokers and many seed-stage AI classifiers present.

name: Cyber and liability premiums being carved out for generative-AI risk (cyber, tech E&O, D&O, GL)

notes.insurgent: Jan-2026 AI exclusions are fresh and unpriced, but AI-specific spend is tiny and Armilla, Klaimee, Corgi funded.
notes.growth: New coverage category created by exclusions, but current spend small; Armilla, Klaimee, Corgi, Mount already funded.

name: India: interest and fees households and small businesses pay on gold-backed loans (banks, NBFCs, informal)

notes.insurgent: RBI gold-loan rules force assaying, auction SOP and LTV monitoring, but Muthoot-class incumbents are strong and Rupeek exists.
notes.growth: Fast-growing $20B interest pool and RBI rule shock, but Muthoot-class incumbents are strong and own-branch rule favors them; Rupeek present.

name: US heavy trucking liability and cargo insurance premiums

notes.insurgent: Carriers' 14-year loss streak and driver shock are real, but Nirvana is $1.5B and MGA path needs reinsurer backing.
notes.growth: Derived split of commercial auto; Nirvana shows leader exists; MGA excess and umbrella is capital and licensing heavy.

name: US feedlot and packer purchases of cattle and calves (cattle cash receipts)

notes.insurgent: Herd at 1951 lows and screwworm are dramatic, but heifer leasing is capital- and biology-risk heavy for a small team.
notes.growth: Primary $134B and historic herd low, no funded players; wedge is cyclical heifer finance with mortality and regulatory risk.

name: US businesses' spend on uniform, linen and workwear rental (incl. healthcare linen)

notes.insurgent: Cintas-UniFirst merger frees accounts for re-bid, no funded startup; but SMB audit ARPU is small and roll-up is asset-heavy.
notes.growth: Cintas-UniFirst merger creates re-bid churn, no funded attackers, but plant-and-route capital intensity blocks a startup; buyer audit small.

name: US residential construction trade labor (payroll and subcontract labor, plus staffing/payroll/training intermediation)

notes.insurgent: Enforcement shrinks labor supply a startup cannot create; classification, E-Verify and joint-employer risk, poor marketplace history.
notes.growth: Real $245B payroll and enforcement shock, but labor marketplaces have a poor record and heavy joint-employer legal risk.

name: SNAP benefits redeemed at US grocers, plus state administration and retailer compliance spend

notes.insurgent: State SNAP food restrictions create an unresolved SKU-eligibility data gap with mandated users; retailer ARPU small, government cycles long.
notes.growth: Vendor-capturable slice is a sliver of $101.7B, buyer is slow government; SKU eligibility data is open but low ARPU.

name: Brazil: farmers' annual crop-input purchases (seeds, fertiliser, crop protection), 72% bought on credit from retailers, manufacturers and cooperatives

notes.insurgent: Record farm-credit stress and retailers lending blind; Traive and Agrolend funded. Brazil execution and credit-risk heavy.
notes.growth: Real ag-credit stress, but lending into defaulting farmers is dangerous; Traive and Agrolend present; $100M needs large credit share.

name: State Medicaid program administration, esp. the H.R.1 work-requirement and six-month-renewal build-out

notes.insurgent: Jan 2027 deadline is hard, but integrators are discounting and government procurement is slow; vendor-addressable slice is small.
notes.growth: Hard Jan 2027 deadline, but shock slice ~$0.7-1B one-time; integrators discounting, free federal EMMY tooling, slow state procurement.

name: US enterprises' spend on offshore-delivered IT services (application development and maintenance, testing, infrastructure from Indian IT majors and captives)

notes.insurgent: H-1B fee and AI deflation hurt Indian IT, but Accenture, AWS and funded startups attack modernization.
notes.growth: H-1B fee and AI deflation are real shocks, but incumbents large and adapting; assumption-derived size; narrow modernization niches funded.

name: Japan shippers' spend on contracted road freight (multi-tier trucking subcontract chain)

notes.insurgent: Jan-2026 law is real, but 60,000 small carriers have no budget. Shippers' CLO plans pay, and Japan market access is hard.
notes.growth: Derivable $110B pool and fresh 2026 law, but Japan-only, Hacobu and T2 funded; wedge is small-carrier compliance SaaS.

name: Craft labor spend on US data-center construction (electricians and allied trades)

notes.insurgent: AI-capex labor shortage is real, but staffing is competitive, Buildforce is funded, and labor supply cannot be created quickly.
notes.growth: AI capex bids up trades labor, but staffing marketplaces are thin-margin and Buildforce funded; prefab electrical assemblies more interesting.

name: US building owners' spend on elevator, escalator and moving-walk maintenance, repair and modernization

notes.insurgent: Otis service quality and cab-phone POTS conversions help, but IUEC labor, licensing and OEM-locked controllers gate entry.
notes.growth: Independent roll-up plausible but $8B pool, mechanic bottleneck, Otis owns WeMaintain; PE would do it first.

name: Private-school-choice money: state ESAs, vouchers, tax-credit scholarships, plus the federal tax-credit scholarship starting 2027

notes.growth: Operator take only $300-500M sector-wide; ClassWallet and Odyssey entrenched; federal credit rules not final.

name: US graduate-school borrowing displaced from Grad PLUS (private lending gap)

notes.insurgent: Grad PLUS closure is certain, but spread revenue is far below loan volume and Sallie Mae, SoFi have capital.
notes.growth: Crisp July 2026 Grad PLUS closure leaves $8B yearly gap, but lender revenue is a spread, credit risk real, Sallie Mae, SoFi, GradBridge respond.

name: US electric utilities' vegetation management (line clearance and tree trimming)

notes.insurgent: Work-verification and unit-price audit has a clear utility payer; Overstory funded and software at 1-2% caps near $75-150M.
notes.growth: $7.5B pool; contractors sell crew-hours so analytics conflict; Overstory, Pano, Gridware funded; audit software near $100M ceiling.

name: US trucking diesel purchasing (fuel cards, discount networks, surcharge pass-through)

notes.growth: Diesel spike is cyclical; intermediary margin only $4-9B; Corpay and WEX entrenched; small-carrier fuel credit is defensible piece.

name: US farm employers' spend on hired and H-2A labor

name: US P&C insurers' claims-handling (adjusting) and litigation-defense expense (LAE)

notes.growth: Primary-derived $86B LAE pool with thin surge capacity; litigation-spend intelligence unfunded but small; claims AI is crowded cliche.

name: US industrial MRO and indirect-supplies spend by plants, contractors and facilities (industrial distribution)

name: US homeowners' residential HVAC replacement and installation (equipment plus labor)

notes.insurgent: Real price-opacity pain, but Jetson and Quilt are funded, shock partly pulled forward, and marketplace plays are capital-hungry.
notes.growth: Large pool, but shock is a demand slump; Jetson funded, PE roll-ups and ServiceTitan entrenched; price-transparency wedge is lead-gen.

name: US data centers' spend on onsite / behind-the-meter power (engines, turbines, fuel cells, batteries, backup) and the services around it

notes.growth: Real scarcity shock but OEMs supply-capped; Crusoe, Bloom, ProEnergy, Emerald funded; unfunded layers are services under $100M.

name: Wholesale, MGA and delegated-authority intermediation of US surplus lines (E&S) and specialty insurance

name: Rural Health Transformation Program state grants

notes.growth: One-time money, five-year cliff, 50 separate procurements, unknown vendor share; consultancies and EHR vendors capture most.

name: Northeast US home heating oil retail (fuel, service contracts and installs)

notes.insurgent: Density death spiral and $450M heat-pump money, but the play is a capital-heavy roll-up of a shrinking base.

name: Rural Health Transformation Program awards (CMS to 50 state agencies to rural providers and vendors)

notes.growth: Duplicate of P063: one-time five-year grants across 50 procurements; vendor-addressable share unknown.

name: US low-income housing tax credit (LIHTC) equity, development and compliance

name: US federal crop insurance premiums (farmer-paid plus taxpayer subsidy)

name: US school districts' spend on student transportation (own fleets and contractor-run yellow bus)

name: US industrial plant maintenance, repair and millwright labor and outsourced machinery repair

name: US electric utilities' spend on vegetation management (line clearance)

name: England adult social care: council purchases from independent home-care and care-home providers

name: US importers' spend on customs brokerage and trade-compliance services

name: Japan home-visit long-term care insurance payments to home-help agencies

name: US workers' compensation system cost (medical, indemnity, claims administration, cost containment)

name: India: health-insurance claims that insurers pay to hospitals and patients

name: US oil and gas operators' produced-water gathering, disposal, recycling and treatment

name: US households' and businesses' spend on structural pest control services

name: US households' and small businesses' fees for tax preparation and accounting (paid preparers and CPA/EA firms)

name: US estate settlement (post-death administration) fees paid by estates and heirs
